newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW Australia summer crops look good - government.
newsitem.headline: NSW Australia summer crops look good - government.

text.p: Harvest of the estimated 254,000 hectares of summer crops in the Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) was progressing well with generally favourable weather, the state's Department of Agriculture said in its Grains Report.
The estimate, which excludes cotton and rice, is up by seven percent on last season.
Excellent average summer crop yields were predicted, it said.
Main summer crops, apart from cotton and rice, are grain sorghum, maize, soybean, sunflower and mungbean.
Preliminary estimates were for the intended sowing of 4.11 million ha of winter crops in 1997 against about 4.02 million ha harvested in 1996, it also said.
Preparations for winter crop sowings were well underway but follow-up rain in many areas in April would be welcome, it said.
Preliminary estimates indicated intended 1997 wheat sowings at 2.7 million ha compared with the 1996 area harvested of about 2.8 million ha.
A forecast 10 percent reduction in anticipated returns for grain produced was influencing planting intentions, it said.
In the record year of 1983, almost four million ha were harvested for the production of nearly nine million tonnes.
Anticipated sowings in the north and south of the state would decline by about five percent, while sowings in the centre of the state would be much the same as last year, it said.
Statewide 573,000 ha could be sown to barley against an estimated 517,000 ha harvested last year and the record of 623,000 ha sown in 1993.
Preliminary estimates for canola sowing were for 206,000 ha, against a harvested area of 147,000 ha in 1996. Seed industry sources suggest plantings would be higher, it said.
In pulses, 1997 winter grain legume sowings would possibly total 146,000 ha compared with 106,000 ha harvested in 1996, it said.
